602: Your fastest nerve signals race along at up to a hundred and twenty metres per second. That's faster than a Formula One car at full throttle.
603: And still, you need roughly a quarter of a second to react. See the ball. Move the hand.
604: You can test this at home. A friend holds a ruler, lets go without warning, and you catch it. Most people let about twenty centimetres slip through their fingers.
605: Quick side note: the delay isn't really the wire. It's everything in between. Eyes, brain and muscles pass the message along like a relay team, and every handover costs a little time.
606: So let's push the dial. Every neuron fires ten times faster.
607: Here's the catch. More firing means more energy, and more energy means more heat. Your brain works best in a narrow temperature range. At around forty degrees Celsius, people already start to get confused.
608: Evolution found a smarter trick. Your brain doesn't think faster. It thinks wider. Around eighty-six billion neurons, all working at the same time.
609: Verdict: speed at maximum is a fever, not a superpower. Back to normal. Next dial: the body.
610: Your brain isn't only a thinker. It's also a very strict bodyguard.
611: In a classic experiment from 1961, researchers fired a starter pistol behind people just as they pulled with all their might. They pulled harder than before. Shouting helped too.
612: Their muscles hadn't changed in that second. Their brains had simply let a little more through.
613: Scientists can even measure the gap. Add a tiny electrical pulse to the nerve during an all-out push, and the muscle often squeezes out a little extra.
614: So, gym test. Same muscles, same bones. Only one change: the bodyguard is fired. Full strength. And while we're at it, no pain.
615: You lift more than ever. Once. Scientists think the bodyguard exists for a reason: tendons and bones have limits too.
616: And no pain sounds even better, right up until you meet people who were born unable to feel it. They often get hurt without noticing, from burns to broken bones.
617: Pain isn't the enemy. It's the smoke detector.
618: Verdict: the bodyguard stays. But one dial on this panel really can go up. And you already own it.
